Trump TV viewership drops to fewer than 100 as White House channel fails to attract audience
item.description: According to a report by the Daily Beast, Trump TV, the White House's newly launched channel intended to replace banned media outlets like CNN and Politico, has experienced a significant decline in viewership. The channel, which was promoted as an 'essential' one-stop shop for Trump-related content, has seen its audience drop from an initial high of 8,500 viewers to a mere 91 viewers during off-peak hours. The report highlights that the channel primarily streams reruns of old speeches and engagements, failing to provide fresh or engaging content that would appeal to even the most dedicated MAGA supporters. The decline in viewership has been exacerbated by an accidental Instagram livestream from former White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt, who drew over 1,000 viewers while live-streaming from her bed with her infant daughter. This incident, which occurred during a Sunday nap, drew significantly more attention than Trump TV's low viewership numbers. The Daily Beast report also no

item.title: Young Mother Suffers Severe Brain Injury in Dublin Collision After Westlife Concert
item.description: A 37-year-old mother of two, Danielle O'Keane, sustained a life-ending brain injury in a road traffic accident on North Wall Quay in Dublin on Saturday night, September 26, 2026, while traveling to meet her husband after attending a Westlife concert at the 3Arena. The incident occurred around 11 p.m. when Danielle, who was with friends, was riding in a rickshaw heading toward the city center. According to her brother-in-law Derek, the rickshaw hit a curb and overturned within seconds, causing a catastrophic brain injury. Danielle was rushed to Mater Misericordiae University Hospital, where she remains in ICU on a ventilator. Medical professionals have confirmed through brainstem testing that her injury is irreversible, and her family is preparing for the difficult decision to turn off her ventilator. The family had been eagerly anticipating a family holiday to Mallorca, scheduled for October 5, 2026, with Danielle's two young sons, aged five and two. Derek described Danielle as a 'hear

item.title: Sanofi and Regeneron deepen partnership for immunology antibody development
item.description: Sanofi and Regeneron Pharmaceuticals have announced an expanded collaboration following the success of Dupixent, a highly effective medication for chronic conditions. The partnership now includes a new series of experimental antibodies focused on immunological diseases. Under the terms of the agreement, Sanofi will pay Regeneron a $1 billion upfront payment, with potential additional milestone payments totaling up to $7 billion. Regeneron will lead the research and development efforts, while Sanofi will handle commercialization. The companies will share profits equally from the resulting medications. George Yancopoulos, Regeneron's chief scientific officer, emphasized the strategic value of combining Regeneron's scientific expertise in antibody development with Sanofi's global commercial reach. The collaboration aims to deliver the next wave of innovation in immunology treatments. This expansion builds on the existing successful partnership that has already produced Dupixent, which has

item.title: Premier League Clubs Demand Swift Sanctions Against Manchester City Following Financial Breach Verdict
item.description: Senior football figures within the Premier League are calling for immediate action against Manchester City following the club's guilty verdict in a financial breach case. The independent commission confirmed that Manchester City had artificially inflated their revenue by over £900 million through 'sham' sponsorship deals between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons. Rival club executives are concerned that delaying the punishment could undermine the integrity of the current title race, especially if Manchester City were to win the championship again. The Premier League has stated its desire for the case to be 'concluded as soon as possible,' though Manchester City has indicated it will appeal the decision, potentially extending the process. The club's chief executive, Ferran Soriano, has suggested the appeal could take a long time, but Premier League regulations stipulate that an appeal should be resolved within 12 weeks. item.title: Trump Repeats False Claim About Winning California in Honest Election
item.description: President Donald Trump has repeatedly claimed that he would have won California in the 2024 presidential election if the state had an 'honest election system,' rather than the current system that includes widespread mail-in voting. This statement, which Trump made during a Wednesday press briefing, has been widely debunked by fact-checkers and historical data. CNN fact-checker Daniel Dale noted that Trump lost California by significant margins in the 2016, 2020, and 2024 elections, with vote margins of over 4 million, 5 million, and 3 million votes respectively. No Republican has won a major statewide election in California since Arnold Schwarzenegger's 2006 gubernatorial victory, and no Republican presidential candidate has carried the state since George H.W. Bush in 1988. Trump's claim is part of a broader pattern of assertions that election results are rigged when they do not favor him, while claiming elections are fair when they do. item.title: Trump's Attack on Powell Likely to Keep Fed Chair in Position, Expert Says
item.description:
President Donald Trump has launched a new public attack on Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell, demanding his resignation or a federal lawsuit over the renovation of the Fed's headquarters. The president's comments, made in a lengthy Truth Social post, cited an inspector general's report that identified 'deficiencies in the management of the renovation project' and claimed costs would reach 'at least 2.5 Billion Dollars, with no end in sight.' Trump blamed Powell for the situation, stating, 'This is Jerome Powell's fault, and he should be forced to resign, IMMEDIATELY!' He also criticized Powell's interest rate policy, calling it 'High Interest Rate Policy (only on 'TRUMP').'
Prominent economist Justin Wolfers, from the University of Michigan, responded to Trump's remarks on X, stating that the president's approach is 'the most effective way to ensure that Jay Powell stays on the Fed.' Wolfers explained that Powell would be unlikely to resign while facing public pressure from the pres

item.title: Tennessee Governor Orders External Review After Execution Mishap Involving Convicted Murderer Christa Pike
item.description: Christa Pike, a convicted murderer in a brutal 1995 killing, experienced a significant medical complication during her execution on Wednesday night in Tennessee. According to court filings by her legal team, Pike continued to breathe for nearly an hour after receiving two doses of lethal injection drugs. This incident prompted the state to halt the execution and initiate emergency medical care. The Tennessee Department of Correction confirmed the situation, stating that Pike was administered two rounds of lethal injection drugs, but she remained conscious and breathing for an extended period. The governor of Tennessee has ordered an outside review of the execution process following this botched procedure. This is not the first time Tennessee has faced issues with executions; the state has a history of procedural errors in capital punishment cases. Pike was convicted for the 1995 murder of a woman in Knoxville, Tennessee, and had been scheduled for execution after years of legal appeals

item.title: Dow Jones Futures Dip as Inflation Data and Micron Earnings Loom Amid AI Stock Resilience
item.description: Dow Jones futures experienced a slight decline early Wednesday, with S&P 500 futures remaining relatively unchanged and Nasdaq futures edging lower. The market's movements were influenced by rising Treasury yields, which caused the stock market rally to soften, though gains were partially regained as crude oil prices decreased. The Federal Reserve's key inflation report was scheduled for release before the market open, while Micron Technology's earnings report was anticipated after the close. Micron's performance was particularly noteworthy, as the company exceeded expectations, driving its stock price higher. Meanwhile, AI-related stocks, including those in the 'Magnificent Seven' group, demonstrated resilience, largely ignoring the upward pressure from Treasury yields. Bloom Energy also saw a significant surge, rising nearly 11%, and joined 18 high-performing stocks that made it to top stock lists. The broader market saw mixed results, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average declining

item.title: Marjorie Taylor Greene's Political Rebranding Under Scrutiny Amid January 6th Controversies
item.description: The article critically examines Marjorie Taylor Greene's recent attempts to reposition herself as a truth-teller and liberal ally, highlighting her history of controversial actions and statements. The author points out that Greene, a former Trump ally, has been making claims about Republicans and her former boss while simultaneously engaging in behavior that contradicts her new image. The piece references her past actions, including her testimony during the House January 6 committee hearings where she sought a pardon for her involvement in the Capitol riot, her joking about the January 6 attack at a New York Young Republican Club gala, and her verbal harassment of Parkland survivor David Hogg. The article also mentions her personal life controversies, such as multiple affairs while married and her obsession with Hunter Biden, which she brought to congressional hearings. item.title: Una Merkel: A Lively Supporting Actress of Hollywood's Golden Age
item.description: Una Merkel (1903-1986), born in Covington, Kentucky, was a prominent American actress known for her lively, wisecracking supporting roles in classic Hollywood films during the 1930s. She began her career on stage in New York before transitioning to Hollywood, where she became a familiar face in numerous films. Merkel's notable performances include her role in '42nd Street' (1933) and a memorable fight scene opposite Marlene Dietrich in 'Destry Rides Again' (1939). Her sharp comic timing and distinctive Southern-tinged delivery made her a standout in roles as loyal friends, sassy sidekicks, and spirited characters. Later in her career, Merkel returned to the stage, winning a Tony Award, and received an Academy Award nomination for 'Summer and Smoke' (1961). The vintage photos featured in the article capture her charm, energy, and distinctive screen presence, highlighting her significant contribution to Hollywood's Golden Age as a memorable supporting star. item.title: Why I'm Building More Local-First Software
item.description: The article discusses the author's growing interest in developing local-first software, which prioritizes offline functionality and user data privacy. The author explains that traditional applications often require constant internet connectivity, leading to functionality loss when users are offline. In contrast, local-first applications keep core functionality and data available on the device, only using the internet for synchronization when connectivity is available. The author provides examples of how note-taking applications could work differently with local-first architecture, where data is stored locally and synchronized later. The article also explores how local-first principles can be applied to AI applications, allowing for privacy-focused tools that don't require uploading personal data to remote servers. The author acknowledges challenges in local-first development including synchronization conflicts, storage limitations, and security considerations, but argues that these can

item.title: Fiona Lowe, Daughter of Actor Chad Lowe and Kim Painter, Dies at Age 13
item.description: Fiona Hepler Lowe, the 13-year-old daughter of actor Chad Lowe and Kim Painter, has passed away, according to a statement released by her family. The family confirmed the news to People magazine on Tuesday, expressing their deep sorrow over the loss of their beloved daughter. In their statement, they described Fiona as 'a loving young girl who was smart, creative, and loved to dance,' and emphasized that she was 'adored by her sisters and deeply loved by her parents,' adding that 'she was the light of our lives.' The family also shared that Fiona was born on November 16, 2012, to Chad and Kim, making her the second daughter in the family. Her older sister, Mabel Painter, is 17, and her younger sister, Nixie Barbara, is 10. Fiona's middle name, Hepler, honors her father's late mother's maiden name and is also shared by her father's brother, Rob Lowe. Chad Lowe, known for his roles in shows like 'Pretty Little Liars' and 'Supergirl,' has won an Emmy for his role as Jesse McKenna on 'Life

item.title: Netanyahu's Pre-Election Warning: Security Concerns or Political Strategy?
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has warned that Israel's enemies may attack before the October 27 election, sparking debate over whether his statement is based on genuine intelligence or a political strategy. During a visit to Tel Nof Air Base, Netanyahu stated there were 'indications' of potential attacks ahead of the election, though security officials later clarified there was no specific intelligence warning of an imminent pre-election attack. The Jerusalem Post reported that Israeli security officials said Israel was on high alert regarding Iran but there was 'currently no specific intelligence warning on the table.' The Times of Israel noted that IDF sources knew of no specific pre-election threat, with alert levels unchanged and no additional troops mobilized. Opposition leader Yair Lapid demanded an emergency security briefing, which Netanyahu provided, though Lapid later stated there was 'no reason to put the public in a panic.' item.title: Furry Community in Aviation Industry: Pilots Maintain Professionalism Amidst Misinformation
item.description: The article discusses a recent speech by Senator Tommy Tuberville, a Republican from Alabama, who made unfounded claims about airline pilots being part of the furry fandom, a subculture where individuals enjoy dressing as anthropomorphized animals. Tuberville's remarks, which were part of an anti-trans rhetoric, suggested that many airline pilots, flight attendants, and air traffic controllers are part of this community, implying a threat to public safety. However, the article clarifies that while there is a notable presence of furries in the aviation industry, the community maintains a clear separation between personal interests and professional duties. Pilots and other aviation professionals who identify as furries emphasize that their fandom is a personal hobby, not something they bring to work. The article cites interviews with several individuals, including Toby, a flight instructor and prominent furry, and Vulan, a pilot who runs a group chat for furries in aviation. They note th

item.title: How Israeli Checkpoints Choke Palestinian Life in the Occupied West Bank | WIRED
item.description: The article details the severe impact of Israeli checkpoints on daily life in the occupied West Bank, particularly focusing on Nablus and Hebron. It describes how checkpoints have become a daily obstacle for Palestinians, causing long delays, disrupting family life, and affecting employment opportunities. In Nablus, commuters spend hours waiting at checkpoints, with some employees sleeping at their workplaces due to the unpredictability of travel times. The article highlights specific cases, such as Ali Haj Ali, who works at Sama Pharmaceuticals and often cannot return home until late at night, and Ohood Khatatbeh, whose town has a single gate that controls all movement in and out. The checkpoint system has led to businesses rejecting candidates who live outside Nablus, as they would face long commutes. In Hebron's Jaber neighborhood, checkpoints have effectively isolated the area, with only one entrance controlled by a military checkpoint, making daily activities like accessing school

item.title: Yankees' Massachusetts Natives Schlittler and Rice Lead Team to 9-0 Wild Card Game 1 Victory Over Red Sox
item.description: The New York Yankees secured a dominant 9-0 victory over the Boston Red Sox in Game 1 of the American League Wild Card Series at Yankee Stadium on September 30, 2026. Massachusetts natives Cam Schlittler and Ben Rice delivered standout performances, with Schlittler striking out 10 batters over 6 1/3 scoreless innings and Rice hitting two home runs, including a grand slam, for a six-RBI game. Schlittler, a Walpole, Massachusetts native who grew up supporting the Red Sox, became a target for Red Sox fans on social media but has since embraced his role as a Yankees pitcher. He threw a career-high 117 pitches, including 77 strikes, and relied heavily on his four-seamer and curveball, allowing only two singles and one walk. Rice, who grew up in Cohasset, Massachusetts, and has long been a Yankees fan, contributed significantly with his offensive output, including a grand slam in the eighth inning. item.title: Ruben Dias Defends Cristiano Ronaldo Amid Team Tension and Fan Interaction Controversy
item.description: Manchester City defender Ruben Dias has addressed recent controversies surrounding Cristiano Ronaldo's behavior during Portugal's international matches. Dias dismissed the media's focus on Ronaldo's recent conduct, including his absence from the lineup against Norway and his reported lack of acknowledgment to fans after a match. Dias emphasized that such incidents are normal in professional sports, stating that players often experience frustration with coaches or situations throughout their careers. He noted that Ronaldo remains a vital part of the Portuguese squad, and the team's focus is on upcoming matches rather than individual incidents. Dias also clarified that the squad does not dwell on such matters, with players like Bernardo Silva and Bruno Fernandes sharing his perspective. The defender shut down inquiries about Manchester City's financial issues, redirecting the conversation to the national team's objectives. item.title: American College of Cardiology Emphasizes Holistic Dietary Patterns for Heart Health
item.description: The American College of Cardiology (ACC) has released a new Scientific Statement emphasizing that overall diet quality, rather than focusing on individual nutrients or foods, is key to maintaining heart health. Published in the Journal of the American College of Cardiology (JACC), the statement highlights the importance of plant-forward eating patterns, limiting highly processed foods, and integrating nutrition into healthcare to prevent and manage cardiovascular disease (CVD). According to the statement, diets should include minimally processed plant-based foods, healthy fats, and proteins while reducing refined starches, added sugars, sodium, unhealthy fats, and low-quality processed foods. The ACC statement notes that suboptimal diet is a major risk factor for CVD, and diet and lifestyle modifications are essential for both primary and secondary prevention. item.title: Understanding and Overcoming Social Anxiety: Identifying Harmful Habits and Effective Strategies
item.description: Social anxiety disorder affects up to 12% of people at some point in their lives, with many experiencing significant challenges in social settings. The article details the experiences of Mary, a university student who struggled with severe social anxiety, leading to depression and isolation. She avoided group settings, felt intense shame after social interactions, and believed she had a fundamental personality flaw. Experts like Neil Greening of the Social Anxiety Alliance UK explain that social anxiety often involves internalizing feelings of inadequacy rather than recognizing it as a treatable condition. The article outlines common signs of social anxiety, including keeping quiet, giving short answers, playing with a phone to avoid interaction, staying on the edges of groups, and sticking to safe topics. It also notes that increased smartphone use and remote work may be contributing to rising social anxiety levels by reducing social interactions. To manage social anxiety, experts rec

item.title: U.S. Treasury granted exception for Trump donor linked to Russian bank deal
item.description: The U.S. Treasury Department secretly approved a special exception for Konstantin Sokolov, a Russian-American businessman and major donor to President Donald Trump's White House ballroom project, allowing him to complete a transaction involving Teghut, an Armenian copper mine, despite the mine's primary creditor, Russia's VTB Bank, being under U.S. sanctions for its role in Russia's invasion of Ukraine. Sokolov's company, Dynamic Frontier Holdings, announced on September 3 that it had obtained the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) approval on June 1 to proceed with the acquisition of Teghut's shares and debt. The Treasury's OFAC, which enforces sanctions, has the authority to grant exceptions for specific transactions that would otherwise be prohibited, provided they are deemed beneficial to both the company and U.S. government interests. item.title: Federal Judge Orders Trump DOJ to Expedite Release of Epstein Files Following Legal Victory
item.description: A federal judge has ordered the Trump Justice Department to fast-track the release of documents related to Jeffrey Epstein's case, including records mentioning President Donald Trump. U.S. District Judge Colleen Kollar-Kotelly of the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia issued a ruling in a memorandum opinion on Wednesday, granting in part a motion for summary judgment from the Democracy Defenders Fund (DDF). The group had submitted three Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) requests to the DOJ in July 2025, seeking records from the department's investigations of Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell that mention Trump or Mar-a-Lago, as well as communications about the Epstein files involving top officials including then-Attorney General Pam Bondi, then-Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche, Emil Bove, FBI Director Kash Patel, and Dan Bongino. item.title: Vogue Williams Denies Having a Nanny, Calls the Term 'Triggering' in Podcast Discussion
item.description: Vogue Williams, the Irish reality star and mother of four, has publicly denied claims that she employs a nanny to care for her children. Speaking on her podcast 'My Therapist Ghosted Me' with comedian Joanne McNally, Williams addressed rumors about her childcare arrangements. She stated, 'I don’t have any of those,' emphasizing that she is honest about her parenting setup. The discussion arose after McNally mentioned that the term 'nanny' is often used as a 'fancy term for childcare,' and many people have childcare arrangements without labeling them as 'nannies.' Williams acknowledged that some celebrities, like Kim Kardashian, may have multiple nannies, but she pointed out that others, such as Tommy Fury, also have nannies yet face criticism for it. She expressed frustration with the judgment she faces, saying, 'I still get that all the time. People are like, “She probably has a chef and a night nanny.” I don’t have any of those. item.title: OpenAI Enhances Agents API with Browser-Based Computer Use Capability, Maintaining Developer Control Over Website Access
item.description: OpenAI has introduced a new capability to its Agents API, enabling developers to run browser-based tasks within a hosted environment while maintaining control over website access, sign-in processes, and result verification. The announcement, made during OpenAI's DevDay event on September 29, 2026, builds upon the Agents API's public beta launch on September 10, 2026. The new feature allows agents to interact with web interfaces through a browser, but it does not replace the existing API structure or require all sessions to operate through a browser. Developers must add a computer-use tool and enable a desktop in an OpenAI-hosted environment before creating browser tasks. A browser task involves creating a session, following its events, sending the task, and handling website access requests as they arise. If a site requires authentication, the application must manage the sign-in process. After the agent completes the task, developers are expected to verify the results, review browser ac

item.title: White House Excludes CNN from Second Presidential Trip Following Judge's Ruling on Ban
item.description: The White House has excluded CNN from the press pool for President Donald Trump's second presidential trip since a federal judge halted the administration's ban on the network. According to a report by NBC News, the White House had initially included CNN in the rotation schedule for the trip, which included stops at a truck plant in Denton, Texas, and a speech in Durant, Oklahoma. However, CNN was notably absent from the daily guidance released for the trip. This exclusion follows a federal judge's recent order that paused Trump's attempt to bar CNN, MS NOW, and Politico from the White House grounds. The judge's ruling, however, only covered access to the White House grounds, leaving the administration room to sideline the outlets elsewhere. This is not the first time CNN has been excluded; over the weekend, the White House kept CNN off Air Force One during Trump's trip to Tennessee, despite the network having been assigned pool duty. item.title: Judge's Ethical Defense of Rule of Law Sparks Reaction to Attorney General's Complaint
item.description:
The news article discusses a legal dispute involving U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche and Minnesota federal judges. The Department of Justice filed a complaint with the Eighth Circuit Court of Appeals against U.S. District Judges Patrick Schiltz and John Tunheim, along with unnamed colleagues on Minnesota's federal bench. The complaint targets comments made by the judges to The New York Times regarding the Trump administration's immigration enforcement policies in Minnesota. The complaint, signed by DOJ officials Stanley Woodward and Trent McCotter, accuses the judges of 'unethical and partisan commentary' and requests they be recused from cases involving the Department of Homeland Security. It also seeks an investigation into judges who 'covet publicity.'

item.title: Conservative CNN Commentator Scott Jennings Exhibits Growing Discomfort Before On-Air Outburst
item.description: Conservative CNN commentator Scott Jennings reportedly became increasingly uncomfortable and disconnected in the weeks leading up to a profane on-air altercation with fellow panelist Adam Mockler in May. According to Mockler, who described the incident on 'The Daily Beast Podcast,' Jennings had been insisting for weeks that the U.S.-Iran conflict was nearing a resolution, despite the war entering a 'pretty bad stalemate.' Off-camera, Mockler noted that Jennings grew progressively less engaged, avoiding conversation and making eye contact, which he described as 'more and more awkward' behind the scenes. During the live segment, Mockler pressed Jennings on the lack of tangible concessions from Iran, prompting Jennings to respond with 'isn't it past your bedtime?' and a comment about masculinity. item.title: Former CIA Officer Warns of Counterterrorism Risks as Trump Administration Reduces Security Measures
item.description: A former CIA officer, Marc Polymeropoulos, a 26-year veteran of the agency, has raised concerns about the current state of U.S. counterterrorism efforts under the Trump administration. Speaking during an interview with national security reporter Michael Weiss for the 'Bulwark Takes' program, Polymeropoulos highlighted the administration's reduction of counterterrorism resources and personnel, particularly in regions like Africa, where ungoverned spaces pose significant security risks. He expressed worry that the U.S. has become complacent about terrorism threats, more than two decades after the 9/11 attacks. Polymeropoulos emphasized that the U.S. government has finite resources, and diverting personnel and intelligence assets from counterterrorism missions to focus on immigration enforcement, such as border security at Home Depot, is making the country less safe. item.title: Speech Pathologist Warns McConnell's Automatic Gestures May Indicate Unhealing Brain Injury
item.description: Senator Mitch McConnell (R-KY) has been observed making automatic gestures such as thumbs-up and waving, which a speech-language pathologist has suggested may mask a likely brain injury caused by oxygen deprivation. Hilary Shae, a licensed speech-language pathologist specializing in concussion and neurological disorders, discussed these observations on 'The David Pakman Show,' emphasizing that she was not diagnosing McConnell but noting concerning patterns. Shae referenced McConnell's reported 'fall with pneumonia' and a 911 call indicating someone was 'down' before CPR was administered, suggesting a period of oxygen deprivation. She explained that McConnell's gestures, such as thumbs-up and hand-waving, are 'stereotypic gestures'—automatic responses often seen in cases of significant brain damage. item.title: Senator Schmitt Used Unverified Texts in Accusation Against Jack Smith Despite Warnings
item.description: According to a report by MS NOW, Senator Eric Schmitt (R-MO) was warned by Republican staff on the Senate Judiciary Committee that the texts he intended to use to accuse former special counsel Jack Smith of perjury were unvetted. Despite these warnings, Schmitt proceeded to use the texts during Smith's testimony before the committee on Tuesday, September 29, 2026. The committee staff had cautioned Schmitt that verifying the information was their responsibility, but Schmitt's team had requested materials linking Smith's investigation of Donald Trump's efforts to overturn the 2020 election to the Fulton County District Attorney Fani Willis' Georgia case. The Justice Department had shared materials with Republican Judiciary staff prior to the hearing, but Committee Chair Chuck Grassley's team excluded the texts from their memo for the hearing. item.title: Multidisciplinary Care Essential for Effective Migraine Management
item.description: Migraine is a complex neurological disorder that affects more than just the head, impacting multiple body systems and significantly disrupting daily life. According to Deirdre Ní Mhórdha of the Migraine Association of Ireland, effective management requires a multidisciplinary team (MDT) approach that addresses the full spectrum of symptoms and their impact on patients' lives. The article emphasizes that migraine affects over one billion people globally, making it one of the most disabling conditions worldwide, particularly for women under 50. Despite its prevalence, migraine remains under-recognized, under-diagnosed, and under-treated. The condition presents with a wide range of symptoms beyond headache, including nausea, dizziness, cognitive difficulties, fatigue, anxiety, depression, sleep disturbances, and even temporary paralysis. These symptoms often persist between attacks, creating a continuous burden. The article highlights the critical role of primary care providers like pharm

item.title: AI Coding Assistants Rarely Verify Software Origins Before Installation Despite Available Security Features
item.description: A comprehensive study involving 1,920 trials across six open-source research projects, including three focused on high-performance computing and three on quantum computing, has revealed that AI coding assistants rarely verify the origins of software before installation. The research, published by Pengyin Shan, found that these assistants opened provenance signals—data confirming software origins—in only nine instances, representing a rate of just 0.5 percent compared to zero in 384 control trials without such signals. Despite the availability of security features like software bills of materials (which list components within a software artifact) and cryptographic signatures (which confirm authenticity), the assistants failed to actively utilize these trust signals during installation processes. item.title: David Pakman Dissects Trump's Misleading Convention Viewership Claim
item.description: Progressive political analyst David Pakman addressed President Donald Trump's recent claim about the viewership of the Republican midterm convention during a segment on 'The David Pakman Show.' Trump had boasted that the convention, held a few weeks prior, attracted 107 million views across all platforms, surpassing the NFL's 25 million viewers. Pakman clarified that Trump's figure combined all platforms, including online streams and clips, while the actual TV viewership was approximately three million, according to Nielsen. He emphasized that comparing the total views across platforms to traditional TV viewership was misleading, stating, 'It's not even that impressive.' Pakman further explained that the NFL drew 20-25 million television viewers, whereas the convention had about three million, making the comparison apples to apples. item.title: Eclipse Foundation Establishes Sovereign AI Foundation to Promote Open Source AI Control
item.description: The Eclipse Foundation, a leading global open source software foundation, has announced the creation of the Sovereign AI Foundation, a vendor-neutral initiative designed to help organizations navigate the complexities of AI dependencies and make more informed decisions about the technologies they rely on. This new foundation aims to connect industry needs with open source AI projects, fostering greater choice and control over critical AI systems. As AI transitions from experimental phases to essential operational and decision-making tools, organizations face challenges in understanding, adapting, and governing the AI technologies they depend on. The Sovereign AI Foundation addresses these concerns by providing a neutral forum where member organizations can share knowledge, evaluate open source alternatives, and collaborate on practical solutions. The initiative launches with 17 founding organizations spanning technology, industry, research, and the open source community, including CEA

item.title: Ted Cruz blocks AI deepfake lawsuit bill, reigniting GOP rift with Marsha Blackburn
item.description: U.S. Senator Ted Cruz (R-TX) has blocked a bill that would allow people to sue over AI-generated deepfakes on the Senate floor, reigniting a long-standing dispute with fellow Republican Senator Marsha Blackburn (R-TN) over AI regulation. According to Politico, Blackburn attempted to fast-track her NO FAKES Act through unanimous consent, a procedure that typically requires no formal vote but allows any single senator to block it by objecting in person. Cruz objected, arguing the bill was not ready due to free speech concerns, including whether AI-generated content like images and videos shared by figures such as Donald Trump on social media, or satirical content from outlets like The Onion, could be mistakenly deemed illegal under the legislation. item.title: Blacktip Sharks Detect and Orient Away from Sounds Up to 243 Feet Away, Study Reveals
item.description: A groundbreaking study conducted by Florida Atlantic University has revealed that blacktip sharks (Carcharhinus limbatus) can detect low-frequency sounds from nearly 250 feet away and precisely determine their direction. Published in Integrative Organismal Biology, the research provides the first quantified evidence that free-swimming sharks can detect and orient away from sounds in the acoustic far field. The experiments, carried out off the Florida coast, involved playing low-frequency sounds ranging from 100 to 800 Hertz to wild sharks in their natural habitat. Researchers used underwater speakers, drones, and calibrated hydrophones to measure sound levels and track shark movements. The sharks reacted to all three low-frequency sound ranges but showed no response to a 10 kiloHertz control sound, which lies beyond their known hearing range. They detected sounds from distances of up to 74 meters (243 feet), substantially farther than previously demonstrated in freely swimming sharks.

item.title: AI Speech Analysis Tool Predicts Biological Ageing Through Vocal Characteristics
item.description: A groundbreaking study published in Science Advances has introduced an AI-powered 'speech clock' that assesses how quickly a person is ageing based on vocal characteristics. Developed by researchers at Adolfo Ibáñez University in Santiago, this innovative tool analyzes over 700 speech features including pitch, talking speed, and emotional content to estimate biological age. The research team recorded 2,928 Spanish speakers from multiple Latin American countries while they completed various speech tasks, including individuals with cognitive impairments and dementia. The AI model successfully distinguished between healthy individuals and those with cognitive issues by identifying a 'speech age gap' - the difference between predicted speech age and chronological age. Large speech age gaps were strongly associated with cognitive decline, suggesting the tool could serve as an early indicator for conditions like dementia. item.title: Butterfly Wing Patterns Create Motion Dazzle Effect to Confuse Predators
item.description: A recent study published in the journal Nature reveals that butterfly wing patterns and flight dynamics create a visual illusion known as 'motion dazzle,' which makes it difficult for predators to accurately gauge a butterfly's speed and direction. The research, led by scientists from the University of Exeter, demonstrates that the stripes and spots on butterfly wings interfere with predators' visual systems, creating false motion cues that disrupt the predator's ability to target and capture the butterfly. This effect is similar to the well-known barbershop pole illusion, where rotating striped poles appear to move upward rather than rotating. The study combined high-speed video analysis of butterfly flight, simulations of nearly 400 European butterfly species, and human interaction experiments with virtual butterflies. item.title: 120-Million-Year-Old Fossil Pushes Back Origin of Marsupial Lineage
item.description: A newly discovered fossil of Archetheridium sinense, a deltatheroidan mammal from China, has pushed back the origin of the marsupial lineage by approximately 10 million years. The fossil, dating to the Early Cretaceous period (120 million years ago), was found in the Jiufotang Formation in Liaoning province, northeastern China. This discovery represents the earliest unambiguous metatherian, the broader group that includes marsupials and their extinct relatives, ever identified. The fossil includes a partial skull, jaws, nearly complete upper teeth, and portions of the limbs and spine, which is rare for early metatherian fossils that are typically limited to teeth or jaw fragments. Researchers from the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology at the Chinese Academy of Sciences, Dr. Hai-Bing Wang and Dr. Yuan-Qing Wang, suggest that Asia, rather than North America, may have been the center of origin for marsupial-line mammals. item.title: The Historic Photograph of Victor Hugo on His Deathbed Captured by Nadar in 1885
item.description: Victor Hugo, the legendary French poet, playwright, and novelist, passed away from pneumonia on May 22, 1885, at the age of 83. By the time of his death, Hugo was a revered national hero who had dominated French literature and politics for over half a century. The day after his passing—May 23, 1885—his close circle called upon his longtime friend, the famous pioneer photographer Gaspard-Félix Tournachon, better known as Nadar. Nadar rushed to Hugo's home on Avenue Victor Hugo in Paris to immortalize the great man one last time. Taking the photograph required careful staging to accommodate the early camera technology and the solemnity of the room. Nadar refused to carry heavy artificial lighting equipment. Instead, his friend Paul Meurice helped him secure permission to throw open the window shutters overlooking the garden. To control the harsh morning sun, Nadar rigged black drapery across the window and tied it to a bedpost. This isolated Hugo's face against a dark, somber background.

The service, initially rolled out on Tuesday, partners with Axis Bank, India's third-largest private-sector lender, to enable Apple Pay functionality for eligible Visa and Mastercard users. This launch comes after years of anticipation, as Apple had been preparing to enter the Indian market, which is dominated by the state-backed Unified Payments Interface (UPI) system. UPI has become the backbone of India's digital payments ecosystem, allowing instant bank-to-bank transactions without the need for physical cards. In contrast, Apple Pay is card-based and requires integration with individual banks and payment infrastructure providers, making a broader rollout more complex. item.title: 3.8 Magnitude Earthquake Shakes Ventura and Los Angeles Counties
item.description: A magnitude 3.8 earthquake was reported on Tuesday evening in eastern Ventura County, according to the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS). The quake occurred at 8 p.m. near the community of Piru, approximately 2.5 miles from Piru, five miles from Simi Valley, seven miles from Moorpark and Fillmore, and eight miles from Castaic and Stevenson Ranch. The earthquake struck at a depth of 6.6 miles, with light to moderate shaking reported in the surrounding areas. The Modified Mercalli Intensity scale rated the tremor as weak to light. Residents in Ventura and Los Angeles counties felt the shaking, with reports indicating the tremor was felt as far east as Palmdale, as far west as Santa Barbara, and as far south as Inglewood. The earthquake was automatically reported by Quakebot, a computer application developed by the Los Angeles Times that monitors earthquakes detected by the USGS. item.description: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccine coverage among older Canadians remains alarmingly low, with only 34% of those aged 75 or older and 21% of those aged 60-74 with chronic conditions reporting vaccination, according to recent government data. The National Advisory Committee on Immunization (NACI) has strongly recommended vaccination for all Canadians aged 75 and older, as well as for those aged 65-74 with increased risk of severe disease. However, provincial funding for these vaccines varies significantly, with some provinces covering only specific high-risk groups or age ranges. RSV, historically viewed as a pediatric illness, causes significant morbidity and mortality in older adults, with approximately 336,000 annual hospitalizations and 14,000 in-hospital deaths among adults aged 65 and older globally. item.title: Early Mental Health Challenges Identified in Newly Diagnosed Epilepsy Patients
item.description: A recent study published in the journal Epilepsia has found that mental health conditions such as anxiety and depression can emerge early in the course of epilepsy, potentially even before diagnosis. The research, conducted by Venus Tang and colleagues, analyzed 21 publications from 10 countries involving 4,728 adults with newly diagnosed epilepsy. The findings revealed that between 11% and 50% of these individuals experienced depressive symptoms, while 25% to 35% reported anxiety symptoms. Two studies using structured diagnostic tools identified clinical depression in 2.9% to 13.3% of newly diagnosed patients and anxiety or neurotic disorders in approximately 25% of cases. The research also highlighted that a significant portion of patients—between a quarter and half—felt stigmatized by their condition, which negatively impacted their quality of life. item.title: Michigan Horse Confirmed Positive for West Nile Virus
item.description: A horse at a stable in Wayne County, Michigan, has tested positive for West Nile virus (WNV), according to an EDCC Health Watch report. The case was reported on September 29, 2026, and is part of the ongoing monitoring of equine diseases by the Equine Disease Communication Center (EDCC), an independent nonprofit organization supported by industry donations. West Nile virus is transmitted to horses through bites from infected mosquitoes, and while not all infected horses show clinical signs, those that do may exhibit flulike symptoms, muscle twitching, hypersensitivity to touch and sound, changes in mental activity, drowsiness, propulsive walking, and spinal signs such as asymmetrical weakness or ataxia. The virus has no cure, but some horses can recover with supportive care, though mortality rates can reach 30-40%. item.title: Dartmouth Receives $20 Million Gift to Establish Home Healthcare Program for Rural Communities
item.description: Dartmouth College and Dartmouth Health have announced a historic $20 million gift from Richard Levy '60 to establish Dartmouth Health at Home, a program designed to revolutionize rural healthcare by expanding access to at-home care for patients and supporting family caregivers. The initiative stems from Levy's personal experience as a caregiver for his late wife Susan, who was diagnosed with Lewy body dementia. Levy's gift will fund three key areas: the creation of a Family Caregiver Institute to provide education, support, and services for caregivers; the delivery of primary and palliative care directly into patients' homes; and research through The Dartmouth Institute for Health Policy and Clinical Practice to document effective care models and measure outcomes. The program addresses a critical gap in U.S. healthcare, where hospital beds are often occupied by patients who could safely receive care at home, particularly in rural communities. item.title: What Happened When I Ate Raspberries Every Day for a Week
item.description: The article details a personal experiment where the author consumed raspberries daily for a week, exploring their health benefits. Raspberries are highlighted as a nutrient-dense fruit rich in dietary fiber (8 grams per cup), vitamin C, vitamin K, iron, magnesium, potassium, calcium, and polyphenols like ellagitannins and anthocyanins. These compounds offer antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, support gut health, and may help regulate blood sugar levels. The author notes that raspberries are low in natural sugar (about 5 grams per cup) and high in fiber, making them ideal for managing blood sugar, particularly for those with insulin resistance. During the week, the author ate raspberries raw, in smoothies, yogurt, and as a chia jam, observing improved digestion and increased satiety. item.description: The U.S. Supreme Court has ruled in a significant decision that permits the Trump administration to restart deportations to third countries, including nations with documented human rights abuses. The Court's Democratic-appointed justices dissented, expressing concerns over the potential for human rights violations. item.title: Understanding ARFID: The Psychiatric Disorder Behind Extreme Picky Eating
item.description: Avoidant/restrictive food intake disorder (ARFID) is increasingly recognized as a psychiatric condition distinct from other eating disorders, with cases rising by 305% from 2018 to 2022. Unlike anorexia or bulimia, ARFID is not driven by body image concerns but rather by sensory sensitivities, fear of eating-related consequences, or low appetite. The disorder often emerges in childhood and can persist into adulthood, affecting individuals of all body types. Research indicates ARFID has a strong genetic component (79% heritability), neurobiological features, and is commonly associated with conditions like autism, ADHD, and gastrointestinal disorders. Diagnosis typically involves clinical interviews and medical evaluations to assess nutrient deficiencies and growth patterns. item.title: Google Transitioning Gemini's Custom AI Assistants to 'Skills' Feature
item.description: Google has announced the discontinuation of Gemini's 'Gems' feature, which allowed users to create custom AI assistants for specific tasks, in favor of a new 'skills' system. The company will automatically migrate existing Gems to the new format starting November 17, 2026, without requiring user intervention. Gems, introduced in 2024, enabled users to build personalized AI tools such as learning coaches, brainstorming assistants, career guides, coding partners, and editors. Users could also create custom Gems for personal needs like running coaches or vacation planners, and share them with others. The migration to 'skills' will allow these custom assistants to function across different AI tasks, though the transition requires users to input a forward slash '/' to select a skill, a feature more suited for technical users than general consumers. item.description: A recent analysis by MS NOW's Zeeshan Aleem highlights a concerning incident involving President Donald Trump's ambassador to China, David Perdue. item.description: Seattle Mariners manager Dan Wilson announced on Sunday morning that he will not return to his role in 2027, following the team's disappointing 2026 season. item.title: Rare Studio Portraits of Madeline Kahn Captured by Jack Mitchell in 1974
item.description: In 1974, renowned American photographer Jack Mitchell captured studio portraits of actress Madeline Kahn in his New York City studio. This session occurred during a pivotal year in Kahn's career, as she starred in two of Mel Brooks' iconic comedies: Blazing Saddles, where she played Lili Von Shtupp and earned an Academy Award nomination for Best Supporting Actress, and Young Frankenstein, where she portrayed Elizabeth. Mitchell was celebrated for his black-and-white portraits of cultural figures, dancers, artists, and actors, which appeared in publications such as The New York Times, After Dark, and Dance Magazine. The portraits from this session feature classic mid-1970s studio lighting techniques, including crisp contrast against dark backgrounds, clean rim lighting, and creative double-exposure methods that combined profile and direct-facing angles. item.title: Washington Urges Canada to Slow West Coast Oil Pipeline Approval Over Environmental Concerns
item.description: The state of Washington has raised significant concerns about the proposed West Coast oil pipeline, urging the Canadian government to slow down its approval process. In a letter dated September 18 to Canada's Minister for Canada-U.S. Trade, Dominic LeBlanc, Casey Sixkiller, director of Washington's Department of Ecology, expressed serious worries about the potential for catastrophic oil spills and the impact on shared ecosystems and the maritime economy. The pipeline, which would transport one million barrels of crude oil daily from Roberts Bank near the Washington border, would double the volume of crude oil exported through the Salish Sea. Sixkiller warned that this increase would exponentially raise the risk of oil spills, with spill response resources on both sides of the border being insufficient for the scale of the proposed project. item.title: Greer Garson's 1940 'Pride and Prejudice' Portraits Highlight Hollywood's Creative Liberties
item.description: The article discusses a collection of 20 portraits featuring Greer Garson as Elizabeth Bennet in the 1940 Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer film adaptation of Jane Austen's 'Pride and Prejudice.' The film, starring Laurence Olivier as Mr. Darcy, marked a significant cinematic interpretation of Austen's work, though it took notable creative liberties from the original 1813 novel. The production opted for elaborate Victorian-style gowns from the 1830s-1840s instead of historically accurate Regency-era costumes, reportedly reusing costumes from other productions like 'Jezebel' to save costs during World War II preparations. Garson, who was 36 at the time of the film's release, portrayed Elizabeth as the eldest Bennet sister rather than Jane, adapting the character to fit her mature, leading-lady presence. item.title: Rising Mortality Rates in Emergency Surgery for US Adults, Particularly in Rural Areas
item.description: A national study presented at the American College of Surgeons (ACS) Clinical Congress 2026 has revealed a 50% increase in mortality rates associated with three common, treatable emergency surgical conditions among US adults aged 18 to 64 between 1999 and 2020. The conditions examined include appendicitis, acute cholecystitis, and abdominal wall hernia with obstruction or gangrene. These conditions typically carry low mortality when treated promptly, but the study found that death rates rose approximately 50% over the two-decade period. The research, based on data from the CDC WONDER Multiple Cause of Death database, analyzed 19,601 deaths among adults in the specified age group. The study highlighted a significant disparity between rural and urban communities, with mortality rates increasing nearly twice as fast in rural areas compared to urban ones. Crown attorney Kate Ashton noted that Webster had a speech impediment, cognitive issues, and poor health, which made him particularly vulnerable. The sentencing hearing, where victim impact statements will be submitted, is set for February 17, 2027. Walsh was remanded into custody following the hearing. The ad, which features a fictional character named Brad—a young white man depicted as a lazy welfare recipient who spends his days playing video games and eating junk food—has drawn criticism for allegedly 'hating young white men.'

item.title: Giant Clam Shell Reveals Pre-Industrial Climate Conditions of Great Barrier Reef
item.description: A groundbreaking study has uncovered that a giant clam shell from the Great Barrier Reef contains a detailed month-by-month record of climate conditions from 200 years ago. The research, led by scientists from the University of Melbourne and James Cook University, analyzed a 58-centimeter clam shell collected from Jiigurru (Lizard Island Group) in the northern Great Barrier Reef. Radiocarbon dating revealed the clam lived between 1785 and 1827, during the end of the Little Ice Age. By examining microscopic daily growth lines and measuring oxygen and carbon isotopes in the shell, researchers reconstructed sea surface temperatures and rainfall patterns from that era. The findings show that 225 years ago, temperatures were 0.6-0.9°C cooler on average compared to measurements from 1995-2015, with summers being 0.9-1.2°C cooler. Winter temperatures remained similar to today. The shell also revealed a clear rhythm between wetter and drier seasons, and climate patterns consistent with El Niño

item.title: Isabella Rossellini: A Lasting Influence in Cinema and Fashion Through the Decades
item.description: Isabella Rossellini, born in 1952, is an Italian-American actress and model, renowned as the daughter of the legendary actress Ingrid Bergman and director Roberto Rossellini. The snake, identified as a Gaboon viper, is not native to North America and is known for having the longest fangs of any snake species in the world. According to the Santa Ana Police Department, the viper was last seen in a tree within a residential area near Main Street and Edinger Avenue. Anyone who spots the snake is urged to contact the police immediately by calling 714-834-4211. The Gaboon viper, which features two hornlike projections on its snout, primarily feeds on rodents and ground-dwelling birds. It is known for striking and holding onto its prey until it dies. item.description: According to Pedro Sousa, executive director of the Portuguese newspaper 'Record', a private agreement between Cristiano Ronaldo and Portugal national team manager Jorge Jesus regarding Ronaldo's playing time has been broken. The agreement, reached in August before the squad announcement, was meant to manage Ronaldo's involvement in upcoming matches rather than rely on him for every game. However, Sousa claims that Jesus did not honor the agreement, as Ronaldo was left on the bench for the match against Norway, despite having been promised 30 minutes of playtime. item.title: The Fascinating, Smelly History of Scratch and Sniff
item.description: The article discusses the history of scratch-and-sniff technology, which allows people to smell scents when they scratch a special coating on paper. This technology has been used in various contexts, including advertising, children's books, and even in the creation of scented greeting cards. The article explores how this technology evolved from its early days to its current applications, highlighting its role in enhancing sensory experiences in print media. It also touches on the challenges and limitations of the technology, such as the difficulty in creating consistent scents and the environmental impact of the materials used. The piece provides a detailed look at how scratch-and-sniff has been integrated into different forms of media and its cultural significance over the years.

item.description: The U.S. State Department is evaluating a proposal to grant state and local officials access to federal passport records to verify the citizenship status of voters ahead of the November midterm elections. According to a Justice Department court filing, the department aims to share information from the Passport Services Records system to ensure registered voters are U.S. citizens, with the goal of protecting Americans' data, deterring fraud, and supporting the integrity of U.S. citizenship. The filing, submitted in a lawsuit brought by the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee against President Trump's executive order on mail voting, states that the State Department will publish a notice in the Federal Register as early as October 22, establishing a new 'routine use' for passport records under the 1974 Privacy Act. item.title: 40 Rescued, 2 Dead After Machete Fight Causes Boat Capsizing Near Puerto Rico
item.description: At least 40 people were rescued in open waters by the U.S. Coast Guard following a boat capsizing incident near Mona Island, Puerto Rico, on Sunday evening. The incident occurred after a machete fight aboard the vessel, which resulted in two fatalities and forced approximately 60 passengers to jump into the water without life vests. Survivors reported that the makeshift boat was carrying around 60 people when the altercation began, leading to the vessel capsizing in the Mona Passage. The U.S. Coast Guard confirmed that rescue operations were ongoing as of Monday evening, with the first four individuals being pulled from the water by a passing boat that noticed the survivors around noon on Monday. item.description: In October 1951, LIFE magazine photographer Lisa Larsen captured a series of portraits of 20-year-old Anita Ekberg, who had recently been crowned Miss Sweden. item.title: UK Climate Committee Warns of Rising Wildfire Risks Amid Record-Breaking Fire Incidents
item.description: The UK's Climate Change Committee (CCC) chairwoman, Baroness Brown, has issued a stark warning that lives will be lost unless the government takes more decisive action to combat the increasing threat of wildfires. This follows a record-breaking number of wildfires in England and Wales during the summer of 2026, with 1,350 incidents reported—over 300 more than the previous year and more than 1,000 more than in 2024. The CCC, established in 2008, has long warned that the UK is unprepared for the changing climate, with longer and drier summers due to global warming increasing wildfire risks. Baroness Brown emphasized that despite years of warnings, 'not enough action' has been taken, and she called for greater investment in specialist firefighting teams, firebreak planning, and early warning systems. item.title: NASA Commits Additional $359 Million to Boeing Starliner After Astronaut Stranding Incident
item.description:
NASA has reaffirmed its commitment to Boeing's Starliner spacecraft despite a series of significant setbacks, including an incident that left two astronauts stranded aboard the International Space Station for nine months. During that mission over two years ago, astronauts Suni Williams and Butch Wilmore were unable to return aboard Starliner due to propulsion system failures, forcing NASA to arrange their return via a SpaceX Crew Dragon vehicle.
On Monday, NASA officials announced an additional $359 million investment in Boeing to fund comprehensive design modifications and enable Starliner to launch on alternative rockets beyond its current launch vehicle. NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman stated that continuing with Starliner represents the fastest path to reliable crewed access to low-Earth orbit, citing both the agency's extensive experience with the program and the substantial taxpayer investment already made.

item.description: The article details the harrowing experience of Maddie Kowalski, a University of Florida sophomore whose nonconsensual videos were shared widely on social media platforms, particularly X (formerly Twitter). The videos, which depicted her in a vulnerable state while heavily intoxicated, were disseminated through a network of anonymous 'burner' accounts, creating what the article terms the 'burnerverse.' This triggered a cascade of harassment, with her videos going viral on X, trending nationally with over 8.5 million views. item.title: Elderly Woman's Eviction After 70 Years Sparks Mass Protests Over Spain's Housing Crisis
item.description: The eviction of 87-year-old María del Carmen Abascal, known as Maricarmen, from her Madrid apartment has ignited widespread outrage and mass protests across Spain, highlighting the country's deepening housing crisis. Abascal had lived in the same home for more than 70 years, inheriting the lease from her parents, until a real estate company that purchased the building in 2018 sought to terminate her contract and raise the rent to four times what she could afford on her pension. Despite legal battles, mediation attempts, and public support, she was forcibly evicted last Wednesday and is now hospitalized while awaiting medical tests. Tens of thousands of people marched through Madrid and other cities including Barcelona, Seville, and Valencia to protest her eviction and demand stronger tenant protections and a ban on evictions when no alternative housing is available. item.description: The Trump administration has filed an emergency appeal with the Supreme Court to reinstate a Bureau of Prisons policy that would end certain medical treatments and social accommodations for transgender inmates. The Justice Department's request comes after a federal district court issued an order last month prohibiting the Bureau of Prisons from enforcing its new rules, which would have stopped providing surgeries, hormone therapy, and social accommodations like chest binders, wigs, or breast padding for inmates diagnosed with gender dysphoria. The policy was initially introduced following an executive order by President Trump at the start of his second term, which prohibited the use of federal funds for medical procedures or treatments for transgender inmates within the federal Bureau of Prisons system. item.description:
Pennsylvania health officials reported 55 new measles cases since Wednesday, bringing the total to 890 cases across 39 counties in 2026. The outbreak has resulted in 173 hospitalizations and four deaths associated with measles, according to the Pennsylvania Department of Health. The agency emphasized that tracking these trends helps inform the state's ongoing public health response and provides visibility into community transmission across the Commonwealth.
Less than 1 percent of reported cases occurred among vaccinated individuals, while 31 percent of cases involved people under 18 years old. The latest figures come as Pennsylvania has been leading the country in measles outbreaks this year. The company's technology involves concentrating sunlight using lenses and refining it into specific wavelengths to generate up to 10 times more power than diffuse sunlight. The laser beam then serves as an 'ethereal transmission cable' that can be directed at satellites needing power. This innovation addresses a critical need for power in space-based data centers and satellite operations, as current solutions rely on limited battery capacity. item.title: The Shape of the Universe: Flat but Possibly Finite
item.description: The universe appears geometrically flat based on measurements of the cosmic microwave background radiation, suggesting it may be infinite. However, this does not definitively prove the universe is infinite, as the observable universe could be just a small portion of a much larger, possibly curved or topologically complex structure. The cosmic microwave background (CMB) provides critical data about the universe's geometry, with temperature variations matching predictions for a flat universe. Yet, the universe could still be finite, with space wrapping around itself in ways that remain undetectable within our observable horizon. For instance, a flat universe could have a cylindrical or toroidal topology, where traveling in one direction might eventually return you to your starting point. Astronomers have searched for evidence of such topological loops in the CMB and galaxy distributions but have found no conclusive signs. item.title: New Research Shows Visible Light Doesn't Accelerate Water Evaporation at Air-Water Interface
item.description: A recent study published in the journal PNAS by researchers from the Max Planck Institute for Polymer Research in Mainz, Germany, has challenged the notion that visible light can accelerate water evaporation through a 'photomolecular effect.' The study directly tested this hypothesis by subjecting pure water samples to various wavelengths of visible light, including blue, green, and red, under controlled humidity conditions. Using a confocal displacement sensor, the researchers measured the water's surface height under 'light on' and 'light off' conditions, finding no measurable change in evaporation rates. This contradicts previous studies that suggested light could enhance evaporation without heating the water. The researchers also examined the microscopic behavior of water molecules at the air-water interface using a surface-specific vibrational probe, which detected no changes in hydrogen bonding or molecular structure under visible light illumination. item.title: Neurologist: Common Memory Lapses Often Caused by Stress, Not Dementia
item.description: Dr. Tommy Wood, a professor of pediatrics and neuroscience at the University of Washington, explains that minor memory lapses such as forgetting names or misplaced keys are often caused by stress or fatigue rather than early signs of dementia. At Strong New York, the city's largest annual fitness and wellness festival, Wood emphasized that memory formation involves three stages: encoding, consolidation, and retrieval. When stressed or sleep-deprived, individuals typically struggle with retrieval—meaning the memory exists but is hard to access in the moment. In contrast, neurodegenerative diseases often prevent the initial encoding of memories. Wood notes that noticing cognitive changes is a positive sign, as it indicates the person is aware of the issue and can seek help. He highlights that at least 50% of dementia cases can be prevented through lifestyle modifications, including addressing heart and metabolic health, hearing and vision loss, and mental health conditions. item.title: The Final Self-Portrait of Christopher McCandless, Found in Alaska Wilderness, 1992
item.description: The final self-portrait of Christopher McCandless, taken shortly before his death from starvation in the Alaskan wilderness in 1992, has been preserved as a haunting historical artifact. McCandless, a 24-year-old who had recently graduated from Emory University, embarked on a journey of self-discovery in May 1990, severing ties with his family, donating his savings, and abandoning his car to travel across North America. Driven by transcendentalist ideals and a desire to escape modern society, he reached Alaska in April 1992, where he took refuge in an abandoned 1946 International Harvester bus near Denali National Park. He survived for approximately 113 days by foraging for local plants, hunting small game, and successfully hunting a moose. However, when he attempted to leave the wilderness in July 1992, he found the Teklanika River swollen with glacial runoff, making it impassable. Maddow referenced a recent incident in the United Kingdom where five men were arrested in connection with suspicious vans near a rural air base, raising concerns about potential Iranian retaliation. item.title: The Dangerous Practice of 'Kissing the Shuttle' in 19th-Century Textile Mills
item.description: In the 19th century, textile mill workers, particularly women, employed a hazardous method known as 'kissing the shuttle' to thread the narrow eyelet of the shuttle, a wooden device used to carry the bobbin across the loom. This technique involved placing the yarn end in their mouths and sucking it through the shuttle's eyelet, a task performed repeatedly throughout the day to maintain the machinery's operation. While practical for keeping the looms running, this practice posed severe health risks. Shutttles were shared among multiple workers and rarely cleaned, making them breeding grounds for contagious diseases, especially tuberculosis, which was prevalent and deadly at the time. The crowded, poorly ventilated mill environments exacerbated the spread of respiratory infections among workers. item.title: Swiss Landscape Painter Johann Gottfried Steffan: A Key Figure in 19th-Century Art
item.description: Johann Gottfried Steffan (1815–1905) was a Swiss landscape painter regarded as one of the most important Swiss landscapists of the 19th century. Born in Wädenswil, he initially trained as a lithographer before moving to Munich in 1833 to study at the Academy of Fine Arts. Under the influence of Carl Rottmann, Steffan shifted his focus to realistic landscape painting, becoming a central figure among Swiss artists working in Munich. His work specialized in idealized mountain and Alpine scenes, drawing inspiration from the Swiss Alps, the Canton of Glarus, Lake Walen, and later from Berchtesgaden and Ramsau. Steffan's carefully observed yet often romanticized landscapes remain valued examples of the Munich School's approach to nature. These works showcase his refined observation and romantic spirit, establishing him as a leading Swiss landscape painter of the 19th century. item.title: Study Reveals Benefits of Gentle 10-Minute Jog for Brain Function and Mood
item.description: A study conducted by the University of Tsukuba in Japan has found that a slow 10-minute jog can enhance brain health and focus. The research involved 24 healthy young adults who completed a 10-minute treadmill run at a slow pace (1.9 to 3.7 mph) and a resting session. After the jog, participants showed improved performance on attention and self-control tests, reported feeling more alert and pleasant, and exhibited increased activity in the prefrontal cortex, the brain region responsible for decision-making and focus. The study, published in Imaging Neuroscience, suggests that even a brief, easy jog can provide short-term cognitive benefits. Dr. Jessica Gray, a family medicine physician, discussed the findings on 'Fox & Friends First,' emphasizing that the gentle movement triggers norepinephrine and dopamine pathways, which help activate the brain's focus and self-control centers. item.title: Timed Pink Noise During Sleep Enhances Brain Waves and Cerebrospinal Fluid Flow in Small Study
item.description:
A small study suggests that precisely timed bursts of pink noise during sleep may strengthen brain activity associated with deep sleep and increase the movement of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). Pink noise is similar to white noise, but it contains relatively stronger lower-frequency sounds, producing a softer sound often compared with a waterfall.
Researchers studied 14 healthy adults while they slept inside an MRI scanner. Using a technique called closed-loop auditory stimulation, the researchers monitored participants' brain waves in real time and delivered a 50-millisecond burst of pink noise when slow brain waves, or delta waves, reached their peak. The stimulation increased the amplitude of these slow waves and was accompanied by larger CSF flow waves.
Slow waves during deep sleep are associated with processes that help the brain and body recover. CSF circulates around the brain and spinal cord and is involved in transporting waste products away from brain tissue. Previous research

item.description: On October 2, 1978, a 25-year-old Tim Allen, then using his birth name Timothy Alan Dick, was arrested in an undercover sting operation at the Kalamazoo/Battle Creek International Airport in Michigan. At the time of his arrest, Michigan had recently implemented a strict law that mandated a life sentence without parole for any conviction involving more than 650 grams of cocaine. Facing the prospect of spending the rest of his life in prison, Allen chose to cooperate with federal investigators. item.title: Fossil Tooth Reveals Atacama Desert Was Once a Wet Habitat 9 Million Years Ago
item.description: A fossilized capybara tooth discovered in northern Chile's Atacama Desert, one of the driest regions on Earth today, has challenged the long-held belief that the Atacama has remained continuously dry for approximately 40 million years. The 9-million-year-old tooth, found in marine sediments at El Morro in northern Chile, provides the first and oldest record of capybara remains in coastal Chile. Researchers from the University of Arizona and other institutions analyzed the tooth and associated fossil evidence, including phytoliths (microscopic silica deposits from plants) and fossils of freshwater crocodiles and fish, which indicate the area was once a wet coastal environment with palm trees and other vegetation. The discovery suggests that capybaras, which are semiaquatic rodents dependent on water and wetland plants, likely migrated along low-elevation coastal corridors around the Andes mountains, rather than crossing the arid highlands. Her energetic performances and technical brilliance set her apart from other female dancers of the era. Though her film career was relatively brief, Powell remains remembered as a true virtuoso of the screen musical. item.description: Governor Gavin Newsom has signed Assembly Bill 2344, introduced by Assemblymember Matt Haney (D-San Francisco), which aims to address the issue of abused and neglected animals being held as evidence in criminal cases for extended periods. The legislation allows shelters to deem seized animals 'abandoned' after a 14-day period, enabling them to be moved into foster care or adoption rather than remaining in kennels for months or even years. Currently, in Los Angeles County, evidence animals can spend three months to nearly a year in shelters while their owners' cases are processed. A 2022 Los Angeles Times investigation revealed that dogs seized in abuse or neglect cases were often confined to kennels without exercise or interaction with volunteers, leading to behavioral issues and making adoption more difficult. item.title: Earth's Inner Core and Mantle Gravitational Interaction Affects Day Length
item.description: Scientists have discovered that a gravitational competition between the Earth's inner core and the mantle is causing subtle changes in the length of days. The research, published in Nature, explains how the inner core's rotation, which differs from the rest of the planet, creates gravitational effects that influence the Earth's rotation speed over decades. The study, led by geophysicist Mathieu Dumberry from the University of Alberta, used seismic data and models of liquid metal flows in the outer core to reconstruct how this interaction has affected Earth's spin between 1964 and 2019. The findings show that the inner core's gravity attempts to align with mass irregularities in the mantle, creating a slow tug-of-war that results in minor accelerations and decelerations in the planet's rotation. item.description:
Iran has called for a diplomatic solution to its conflict with the United States and Israel after President Donald Trump said he had rejected an Iranian proposal aimed at reopening the Strait of Hormuz and ending the fighting. Iran presented the proposal at the United Nations General Assembly in New York and said it had been transmitted to U.S. representatives through Qatari mediators. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran’s conditions for reopening the strategically important waterway remained unchanged and that only a negotiated agreement could resolve the current deadlock.
Trump said he rejected the proposal, arguing that Iran was seeking an immediate agreement on the Strait of Hormuz because it was under severe pressure. item.title: Human Evolution Shifts Toward Cultural Adaptation Over Genetic Change, Researchers Propose
item.description: Two researchers, Timothy Waring and Zachary Wood from the University of Maine, propose that humans are entering a new phase of evolution where cultural systems increasingly drive adaptation rather than genetic evolution. Their 2025 paper in BioScience argues that cultural inheritance—through medicine, education, technology, and institutions—can respond to adaptive challenges much faster than genetic mutations. For example, medical interventions like eyeglasses or cesarean sections alter biological outcomes without waiting for genetic changes to spread through populations. The researchers suggest this trend is accelerating, with cultural solutions preempting genetic evolution. They also introduce the concept of a 'cultural superorganism,' where human societies function as integrated units of adaptation, similar to ant or bee colonies. item.description: The full harvest moon will reach peak illumination at 10:49 a.m. MDT on Saturday, September 25, 2026, according to EarthSky. The best time to view the moon will be just after sunset on Saturday. Saturn will also appear near the full moon from Friday to Monday, offering sky-gazers a special celestial display. Saturn will reach opposition on October 4, 2026, when it will be positioned opposite the sun from Earth, making it appear larger and brighter in the sky. This opposition marks the optimal viewing period for Saturn. Neptune will also seem close to the moon, but it is much harder to see without binoculars or a telescope and clear, dark skies. The harvest moon, traditionally known as the corn moon, is named for its timing near the autumnal equinox, which occurred on September 22, 2026. Farmers historically used the moon's brightness to continue harvesting crops after sunset. The moon often appears with an orange glow near the horizon due to Earth's atmosphere.
